summary: This bill amends federal criminal law to make it a crime punishable by up to 5 years in prison for a doctor to perform an abortion without first checking for a fetal heartbeat according to standard medical practice, informing the patient of the results, or after detecting a heartbeat, except when necessary to save the mother's life or in cases of rape or incest that meet specific counseling, reporting, and documentation requirements.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends federal criminal law to prohibit certain abortions but contains no provisions related to appropriations, budgets, or government expenditures of any kind.
The bill makes no changes to tax law, rates, deductions, or revenue collection.
While the bill regulates a medical procedure, it does not address public versus private healthcare systems, insurance coverage models, or market structures in healthcare delivery.
No provisions relate to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill does not address immigration policy, borders, visas, or protections for non-citizens.

The bill directly amends federal criminal code to prohibit physicians from performing abortions once a fetal heartbeat is detectable (with narrow exceptions for life of the mother and certain rape/incest cases). This constitutes a substantial federal restriction on abortion access.
No provisions concern military or defense spending or policy.
The bill contains no environmental, regulatory, or climate-related measures.
No provisions affect welfare programs, food assistance, or other safety-net entitlements.
The bill does not address schools, funding, choice programs, or federal education policy.
No provisions relate to controlled substances, decriminalization, or enforcement.

The bill creates a new federal criminal offense (with penalties of fines or up to 5 years imprisonment) for physicians who perform prohibited abortions. This engages criminal enforcement mechanisms, though the primary purpose is abortion restriction rather than broad criminal-justice policy.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
The bill has no fiscal impact or provisions concerning deficits or debt reduction.
The bill does not address legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions concern foreign assistance or international aid.
The bill contains no election, voting access, or electoral-integrity measures.
No provisions relate to technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
The bill does not address worker protections, union rights, or employer flexibility.
The bill includes medical and documentation exceptions but does not create or prioritize religious exemptions versus anti-discrimination rules.
